visualReview.notes: Compared the paired bell towers, open belfries, masonry drums, ochre finish, central carved portal, and tiled nave dome with the accepted archive prints. Verified that the corrected domes join the belfries and the principal cloister remains open.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Checked plaster, limestone plinth, carved stone surrounds, timber door and tiled roofs from street level and from the cloister. The fountain and arcades were visible in the geographic close views.

mediumFiReview.notes: The towers, lanterns, dome, lower convent wing and main court outline remain legible across all four runtime levels. Closer levels resolve the bells, cornice strips, portals and two tiers of arcades.

terrain.grade: The original Copernicus GLO-30 field at the plaza approach is 162.6872 m EGM2008. The 202 m crop ranges from 154.5415 to 171.8472 m and includes urban roof returns. It lacks surveyed grades for the courtyard and doorstep.

geographicReview.notes: The geometry follows the named monastery and the separate mapped outlines of the main basilica, convent and adjoining Chapel of the Miracle. Preserves the principal courtyard ring and the plaza-facing orientation. Geographic load and unload passed.

fidelityReview.scope: The standing main Basilica of San Francisco in Lima, its adjoining Franciscan convent and open principal cloister, and the attached Chapel of the Miracle.
fidelityReview.notes: The contemporaneous architecture, mapped footprint and open court drive the reconstruction. Tower heights, roof links, detailed carving and later repairs are approximated. The separately mapped Church of La Soledad and the subterranean catacombs are outside this model.

imageryReview.notes: Started with the published Qualla gallery. Used three byte-exact public-domain Library of Congress scans of the Courret Hermanos albumen prints published in 1868. The surviving rights record and published volume were verified. The incompletely sourced painting reproduction was excluded.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Inspected the final set of exterior, shared, source terrain and four detail-level views.

limitations: Draft exterior: approximate photographic proportions and simplified ornament. It is not a survey, photogrammetric reconstruction or approved current geographic replacement.

Three published 1868 albumen prints show the front towers and portal, side silhouette with the nave dome, and two tiers of arcades at the principal cloister. Numerical map measurements anchor the horizontal plan.
Terrain sampling/contact, geographic alignment and site activation remain pending. Runtime LODs are produced by the registered after-import pipeline and require visual review.
Reference photos remain in the local Qualla corpus; only provenance, paths and hashes are retained here.
